transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
President Trump heads to Asia this week for a historic meeting in China
with President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
But first, he's visiting the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit.
Diane Desierto is a professor of law and global affairs at the University
of Notre Dame.
>> I think it signals the strategic importance of this particular summit
where a number of crucial decisions will be made.
The visit is extremely important to give it that kind of commitment.
But also, I think, as part of assurances given the amount of investment
that is up for decision-making at this summit.
>> Speaking there to NPR's Weekend Edition.
The FAA is examining Friday's ground stop that's still disrupting some flights.
NPR's Eva Berger reports Transportation Secretary Stron Duffy says it started
with a contractor's work on old copper wires.
L3Harris and the work they were doing updating those wires at a remote facility.
>> NPR reached out for comment from L3Harris.
In a public statement, the company said that it has been working with the FAA
to convert those old wires to a fiber optic system.
And it says it has completed more than 70% of those conversions.
L3Harris said it is supporting the FAA in their investigation.
In a video on the company's website, L3Harris touts the work the company is doing
to update the FAA's communication systems.
>> The brand-new air traffic control system will enhance safety, reduce delays,
and pave the way for new technologies like flying taxis and drones.
>> The website also says its FAA telecom infrastructure supports 45,000 daily flights.
Eva Berger, NPR News, Washington.
>> Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland will challenge Chuck Schumer
to lead Senate Democrats.
Both men have decades of experience on Capitol Hill.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has more.
Schumer's been in elected office in Washington for 45 years, Van Hollen for about 25.
But the Maryland Democrat, who's run Democrats' campaign efforts in both chambers
and is a former deputy to Speaker Nancy Pelosi,
is positioning himself as a change candidate.
He's got some high-profile backers in his corner, including Abdul El-Sayed
of Michigan and Bernie Sanders of Vermont.
But he'll need nearly 30 Democrats in a secret ballot vote to get across the finish line.
For now, Leader Schumer's projecting confidence he's led Democrats for a decade
and said he has the support necessary to secure reelection as leader.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Washington.
>> U.S. futures contracts are trading higher at this hour.
Dow futures are up about 52 points.
NASDAQ futures are up about a half percent.
That's a gain of 139 points.
You're listening to NPR News.
A nearly 100-year-old Georgia O'Keeffe painting that was found in New York City is going
up for auction this week.
NPR's Shonda Lee Stuster has more.
The painting from 1930 that has been buried in a New York City closet
for decades will go up for auction on Tuesday.
The family of the woman who owned the painting said they believed it was a graduation gift
from the 1960s.
The long-lost O'Keeffe works shows a New Mexico landscape with hills and earth-toned colors.
It has been on display at Christie's in New York since early November.
Tylee Abbott, senior specialist and international director of American art at Christie's, said
in a statement that finding a painting by such an acclaimed artist is "a once-in-a-lifetime
moment."
The painting is estimated to sell for more than $3 million at Christie's during the auction.
Shonda Lee Stuster, NPR News.
>> At the weekend box office, Johnny Depp is back on top with Ebenezer, his first studio
movie in eight years.
The Paramount Pictures release took the top spot with an estimated $19 million in ticket
sales with $42 million globally.
That's against a reported $38 million production budget.
In second place, The Cat in the Hat with $11 million, followed by Godzilla minus zero in
third place with $8 million.
And routing out the top five, Ramayana, Rise of Legend in its second weekend with $5.5
million, and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything with Just Under $5.5
million.
You're listening to NPR News.

topics.text: Trump visits the Philippines for ASEAN Summit ahead of China meeting with Xi and Putin
FAA investigates Friday ground stop; Transportation Secretary Duffy blames contractor L3Harris's copper wire work
Senator Chris Van Hollen to challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leadership
U.S. stock futures trade higher, with Dow futures up about 52 points
Georgia O'Keeffe 1930 New Mexico landscape painting found in New York closet goes to auction at Christie's
Johnny Depp's Ebenezer tops weekend box office with an estimated $19 million
